title: Award-winner to fourth choice - what has gone wrong for Ramsdale?
description: From challenging for the Premier League with Arsenal and playing for England, Aaron Ramsdale is now Southampton's fourth-choice goalkeeper.
fullText:
In April 2023, Aaron Ramsdale was within touching distance of winning the Premier League with Arsenal.

But the goalkeeper made a costly error for the Gunners to give away the opening goal in a 3-3 draw with Southampton at Emirates Stadium which contributed to the demise of Arsenal's 2022-23 title bid.

If Arsenal had won that game, the title would have been in their hands. Instead, the draw handed the initiative to Manchester City, who took full advantage.

It was a mistake which perhaps also signalled the beginning of the end for Ramsdale under Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

Four months later, the north London club brought in David Raya from Brentford and the Spaniard quickly claimed the number one spot.

And in a somewhat unfortunate poetic twist, it is the Saints where Ramsdale finds himself completely out of favour three years on as the fourth-choice goalkeeper at a Championship club.

From an England international on the cusp of greatness, Ramsdale is now in the almost unthinkable situation of being without senior football this season in the prime of his career at the age of 28.

So why has Ramsdale had such a fall from grace and where have things gone wrong?

Questions were raised among the Arsenal fanbase when the club paid £24m to sign Ramsdale from Sheffield United in August 2021 after the Blades had been relegated from the top flight.

But he quickly won supporters over by producing a string of excellent saves in his debut season, perhaps most notably against Leicester City when he denied a James Maddison free-kick at full stretch - a save which Peter Schmeichel described at the time as "the best I've seen for years".

After ousting Bernd Leno, his efforts helped Arsenal finish fifth in 2021-22, improving on an eighth-placed finish the previous year.

The following season, Ramsdale was a vital cog in Arsenal's spine as they launched a surprise title challenge, only to be outdone by an imperious Manchester City side.

Despite his blunder in the draw with Southampton - which was one of several results that dented Arsenal's title hopes - Ramsdale made the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) team of the year and was also named goalkeeper of the year at the London Football Awards.

But Ramsdale quickly fell behind Raya in the pecking order in 2023-24 and lost his starting berth after just four league games.

And in one of the only two other Premier League matches he did play that season against Raya's then parent club Brentford, Ramsdale made another mistake to allow Yoane Wissa to put the Bees ahead.

Arsenal recovered to win that game 2-1 in March 2024. But Ramsdale never played for the club again.

He was sold to Southampton for £25m in August 2024 after returning from Euro 2024 with England, having been an unused sub throughout the competition in Germany.

At the time of Ramsdale's signing, he looked to be the perfect goalkeeper and a coup for Southampton.

Russell Martin's side had just won promotion and were hoping to implement a style of play in the Premier League that had brought them such success the previous season.

Ramsdale ticked all the boxes as a goalkeeper who had ability with his feet to complement Martin's preference to build up from the back.

His previous spells at Sheffield United and Bournemouth also justified his addition as someone whose stock had continued to rise despite being involved in relegations.

Ultimately, though, the move to Southampton did not work out as planned.

He made 30 league appearances for a Saints side which finished bottom of the Premier League with just 12 points - the second-lowest ever points tally in the competition - and conceded more goals (66) than any other goalkeeper in 2024-25.

That is not to say Ramsdale was to blame in a Southampton side which performed poorly across the board, with some fans at the time in fact praising him for keeping the score down in games.

It would, however, be the fourth relegation Ramsdale had suffered, having already done so with Chesterfield, while on loan in 2017-18, the Cherries in 2019-20 - although he was named player of the year for Bournemouth that season - and then the Blades.

After signing from Sheffield United in 2017, Ramsdale was an understudy to experienced goalkeeper Asmir Begovic at the Vitality Stadium for two years before his breakthrough.

"First of all, Aaron's a fantastic goalkeeper," Begovic told BBC Sport.

"We first worked together about nine years ago and since then he's been on an incredible ride where he's performed at the highest level.

"I remember my remit when I came into Bournemouth was to mentor and set a tone for some of the younger goalkeepers, one of which was Aaron Ramsdale.

"There's many different factors that go into it but I think it's been unfortunate that maybe a few things haven't aligned for him [at Southampton]."

Southampton's relegation prompted Ramsdale to seek top flight football once more and he moved to Newcastle United on loan for the 2025-26 campaign.

But again, what was supposed to be a move to help re-establish his career at the highest level did not come to pass.

Ramsdale kept just two clean sheets in 23 appearances in all competitions for the Magpies, featuring only 12 times in the Premier League - and neither he nor Nick Pope could make the number one spot permanently their own.

He also had the unfortunate experience of letting in seven goals in one game in a 7-2 defeat by Barcelona in the Champions League last-16 - the most he has ever conceded in a single game.

Subscribe and listen for everything you love about the Saints

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert has seemingly made it clear Ramsdale is not part of his plans this season, with Daniel Peretz his number one, George Long the second choice and Jamie Jones returning to the club as mainly a training goalkeeper.

"The reality is that Rambo's story with the football club started before myself," Eckert told BBC Radio Solent.

"We've had honest conversations from the first day of pre-season until the very last day of the transfer window.

"The expectations for him are clear to support the team in the best way and he's been very professional in doing that so far."

Despite his exclusion so far this season, Ramsdale is said to have a good relationship with Eckert, the coaching staff and the other goalkeepers - and has an affection for the club.

Ramsdale also believes there is a route back into the first team for him at St Mary's and is willing to fight for his place until at least January, when the winter transfer window opens.

He had offers on the table in the summer to go on loan to clubs in England, Spain and Italy but declined, with his current ambition to try to help Southampton win promotion back to the Premier League and play in the top flight.

As well as being a popular figure in the dressing room and well-liked by Saints supporters, Ramsdale also had personal factors to consider for what would have been a move to a fourth club in four years.

His wife recently gave birth to their second child and the family are settled in the area, with Ramsdale only wanting to change clubs if it was the right opportunity.

Begovic says his former team-mate will be finding his current lack of playing time "very difficult and frustrating".

"I had a few spells where I was frozen out at a club for a short time but I can't really relate to Aaron's situation," he added.

"I can imagine there will be some factors that are out of his hands. In the meantime he'll have to make sure that he trains well and stays fit and be ready if an opportunity comes up to play.

"He has to be ready for the long term and if the chance to move elsewhere comes up, he's ready.

"I'd love to see Aaron playing again and hopefully it happens in January but I'm fully aware that it won't be a straightforward situation."

title: Buttler out of tri-series while England prepare central contracts
description: Wicketkeeper Jos Buttler will miss England's 50-over tri-series in Pakistan next month, with Jordan Cox set to be given another chance to impress in his place.
fullText:
Wicketkeeper Jos Buttler will miss England's 50-over tri-series in Pakistan next month, with Jordan Cox set to be given another chance to impress in his place.

Buttler, 36, has been ruled out with the hamstring injury suffered while batting in Thursday's second one-day international against Sri Lanka at Headingley.

Coach Brendon McCullum said it is "hard to judge" how long Buttler will be out for and confirmed Cox will take his place for the series against Pakistan and Sri Lanka, which begins on 20 October.

"We know Jos is an incredible athlete, we know he is supremely fit and is an ultra-professional," McCullum said.

"He will do everything he can to be back as soon as possible."

England also tour Australia for white-ball matches in November - where they are considering playing warm-up matches - as they look to add to their six series wins in limited-overs cricket this year and build towards next year's 50-over World Cup.

They will finalise their squads on Monday with the latest batch of central contracts also set to be announced in the coming days.

Durham opener Emilio Gay is in line for a first deal after his debut Test summer, putting him in line to tour South Africa this winter, while Cox, Tom Banton, who scored his first international century on Sunday, and all-rounder Dan Lawrence could also feature.

Contracts held by former captain Ben Stokes and Mark Wood are set to end after their international retirements. Ollie Pope, Zak Crawley, Matthew Potts and Luke Wood are all out of favour and their one-year deals are due to run out.

Spinner Shoaib Bashir is another intriguing name in that category. He played two Tests against New Zealand and was picked in the Test squad to play Pakistan but did not make an XI as England preferred a four-man pace attack.

England are learning - these are the World Cup issues they need to solve

In a breakout international summer, Cox impressed by scoring fifties in all three Tests when picked to bat number three against Pakistan. He also hit 76 against Sri Lanka when deputising for Buttler in the third ODI at The Oval on Sunday.

"I thought it was quite a Jos Buttler innings," McCullum said.

"He has done really well domestically for a number of years and has been unlucky with injuries.

"For him to have the type of summer he has had and be in the position he is in, he deserves it.

"He is a phenomenal talent, is very well liked in dressing room as well and seems to be one of those guys who is good at everything he does, which will be incredibly annoying."

England will also make a decision on whether to pick bowler Brydon Carse to tour Pakistan. He has not been selected since being arrested then de-arrested on a night out in Derby in August.

After a police investigation ended without action, he is now subject to a Cricket Regulator investigation and, while he remains available for selection, white-ball captain Harry Brook said last week he needs time away from the international scene.

McCullum, who began the summer as England's coach across the three formats before being sacked from the Test role in July, dismissed any suggestion of regret at the end of the English season.

"I loved coaching all three formats," he said. "Things move on, times change. I am biased but I genuinely think [new Test coach] Stephen Fleming will do an unbelievable job with the red-ball side.

"With the extra bit of time it probably does allow you to drill down on a few aspects you have identified you need to improve or shape things differently to get to where you want to."

title: Man City rule breaches not my concern - Mancini
description: Roberto Mancini says an alleged "double contract" during his time as Manchester City manager is "not my concern".
fullText:
Roberto Mancini says an alleged "double contract" during his time as Manchester City manager is "not my concern" after the club were found guilty of breaking the majority of the financial rules they were accused of breaching.

The 115 charges brought by the Premier League against City included 14 instances of failing to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from 2009-10 to 2017-18.

That period covered Mancini's three and a half years in charge, during which he won the FA Cup in 2011 and City's first top-flight title for 44 years in 2012.

Mancini, the current Italy manager, was asked during a news conference before Monday's Nations League game against Turkey about the allegations relating to his remuneration as City manager.

"Found guilty of what?" he said. "It's not an issue that concerns me. It's nothing new because this matter has been discussed for the last four or five years.

"Manchester City has not been found guilty, and the alleged double contract is not my concern. It's their issue, not mine."

German newspaper Der Spiegel had previously accused City of paying a "significant portion" of Mancini's compensation "by way of a fictitious consultancy contract".

It alleged that Mancini was paid more by City for his role as a consultant to Abu Dhabi club Al Jazira than he was getting from his role as City manager, excluding bonuses and incentives.

On Friday it emerged that an independent panel had found City guilty of all but one count of charges brought against them by the Premier League, although sanctions have yet to be determined.

The Premier League declined to comment, while City released a statement saying the "Premier League process remains ongoing with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality".

It added: "The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

Other Premier League clubs are believed to have been informed about the decision and have sought legal advice over possible compensation claims.

City were charged with more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules following a four-year investigation in February 2023.

The club was referred to an independent commission. A behind-closed-doors hearing began in September 2024 and ran for about 12 weeks.

fullText:
Exclusive: Instructors at tech training company Multiverse hit out at ‘remorseless’ and ‘unnerving’ monitoring system

Teachers at Euan Blair’s £1.6bn tech training company, Multiverse, have blown the whistle about “horrendous stress” and feeling constantly watched after bosses started using AI models to surveil and rate their teaching.

Staff delivering apprenticeship training in computer and AI skills to thousands of UK public and private sector workers now have transcripts of online classroom sessions analysed and scored by an AI programmed to alert human managers when they are suspected of doing things wrong.

The AI is trained to flag problems in their performance ranging from not fixing a disruption to the online connection quickly enough – within about a minute – to using too many “filler” phrases, such as “sort of” and “kind of”.

Teachers called the newly introduced system “remorseless” and “unnerving”, and said some staff were on edge, losing sleep, and seeking therapy.

Multiverse was co-founded by the eldest son of the former prime minister Tony Blair and employs more than 800 people. It supplies AI and digital skills training to workers in the NHS, local councils, universities and the private sector, mostly funded through the government’s apprenticeship levy.

Alongside his father, Blair is one of the biggest cheerleaders for wider AI adoption in the UK economy, claiming last week that “every single worker is going to need to be retrained” and that employers want their workforces “as AI-pilled as possible”. Multiverse uses a mix of AI models including Anthropic and OpenAI products.

Its new AI teacher monitoring system tags each instructor by their “risk status”, calculates a “percentage confidence score” and produces written comments about teachers’ work for managers to see at a glance.

It is only the latest example of employers using AI to track worker behaviour. Earlier this year Burger King started using AI to track restaurant workers’ customer interactions and this summer Meta paused tracking of employees’ computer keystrokes amid data privacy concerns and a staff backlash.

With critics warning AI monitoring risks eroding human agency, one study has suggested it can backfire by turning workers rebellious and new research to be published this week reports that workers in the wider UK tech industry are finding AI degrades work satisfaction. The United Tech and Allied Workers branch of the Communication Workers Union concluded AI causes “cognitive surrender” as workers lose skills and confidence and often intensifies rather than eases work.

“Since all of this has come in, the stress level has been absolutely horrendous,” said one of several Multiverse teachers who spoke on condition of anonymity. “It has affected sleep, and not just for me. I’ve gone through a lot of things in my life, and I haven’t ever been in a position where I’m waking up in the middle of the night.”

Previously instructors were observed monthly by a human manager but are now watched for several hours per day by an AI. It is trained to consider marking instructors down if they give vague or uncertain answers to questions, if learners go quiet when asked to contribute and if the teacher gets pulled into a prolonged one-to-one exchange that sidelines the group.

“This is inducing stress because you consistently have to be cautious,” one teacher said. “Your attention is no longer delivering [the lesson] and listening to the learner [but] am I saying the right thing so the AI doesn’t mark me down for something stupid that I’ve mistakenly said.”

Another teacher called it “very uncomfortable”.

Multiverse says the AI does not replace human judgment but “directs human time to where it’s needed most” by highlighting problem. A spokesperson said it was “using AI to improve the experience of learners and customers”, and that only human managers wrote teachers’ performance reviews.

They did not directly address complaints the system caused stress and anxiety and felt “remorseless”, but said its introduction was communicated in advance and teachers will have access to the data the AI collects.

“This agent provides instructors with improved advice on development and feedback – exactly how any learning organisation should be deploying AI,” the spokesperson said. “The most consequential performance management action it can take is to recommend that a human personally reviews a session.”

Blair owns a large minority stake in Multiverse, putting his personal net worth at an estimated £350m. The company was recently valued at £1.6bn albeit on a turnover of £118m and losses of £28m last year. In February, Ofsted, the UK education inspectorate, found Multiverse failed to meet expected standards in several areas, but praised the instructors as “skilled, effective teachers”.

Its new AI monitoring agent, introduced in recent weeks, is trained to spot signs an instructor has not fully internalised the teaching material. The AI is instructed to count verbal tics that point to that conclusion and to “judge the PATTERN across the whole transcript, not isolated instances”.

It says: “1-2 hedges or filler words in an otherwise direct, well-internalised explanation do NOT fail this standard … What fails the standard is a PERVASIVE REPEATED pattern of filler, hedging or re-explanation.”

When a trainer is setting a task “if the instructor is visibly confused themselves or had to self-correct while giving the instruction, that confusion itself counts as evidence the instruction was not clear the first time”. The AI is told to apply a negative mark “even if it was eventually straightened out”.

The workers said the AI monitoring has led to managers pulling them up for suspected “digressions” when in fact they were answering a student’s question.

“It’s impossible for me not to be affected by this mentally,” one teacher said.

“I feel like I’m under continuous scrutiny,” another said. “It’s all about what I didn’t do in this session rather than what I did do. Did I do something incorrectly yesterday? What will I mess up on today? It’s remorseless. I don’t know why this is happening.”

John Chadfield, national tech officer at the CWU, said the public would be horrified to hear of bosses “deploying deeply intrusive surveillance on workers” but said “this news won’t surprise tech workers who feel the reality of the tech sector – an industry in serious need of further regulation.”

He called for new laws to ensure AI is deployed in a socially responsible way and not to “shut off job opportunities for young people, degrade the craft of skilled workers and make astronomical profit for a few”.

Being constantly monitored by an AI is deeply uncomfortable. Imagine every word you say on the job being checked against a rubric that dictates what you’re expected to say and how. That’s the reality for me and my colleagues: every session we deliver to apprentices is now recorded and transcribed. It feels intrusive. Multiverse calls it quality assurance, but it feels like surveillance.

Managers can now look at a dashboard showing how the AI has judged each of our sessions. It assigns a risk level to each of us: the risk of not having said the right things. That’s stressful, for several reasons.

First, the AI isn’t always accurate. Managers are now tasked to investigate trainers for not following the script – at least according to the AI – when actually they were adapting the lesson to a learner’s needs. The threat of being questioned in such detail, at any time, is a constant source of anxiety.

Second, there is no transparency. During the rollout, all delivery staff were kept in the dark while the system was developed. We have no insight into the AI’s analysis. The company says staff will get dashboard access in time, but for now only managers can see it.

The need to always be cautious warps your priorities. Instead of focusing attention on the learner, you become obsessed with whether you’re saying the right thing. Being on camera for most of the day is stressful in itself; being haunted by an AI makes it worse.

A more productive way to use AI would be to improve the teaching materials and raise the standard of what we teach. Instead, the AI is checking whether the teacher managed to fill the gaps? As it stands, this is surveillance, not empowerment.

And I’m worried about what this data is for. In a climate of AI replacing people, I can’t help but worry it will be used to train AI to replace coaches and instructors altogether. Apprentices don’t want that and neither do I, and I would never consent to my sessions being used this way.

fullText:
Company behind Claude chatbot expected to attend separate Australian government hearing on AI next week

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The chief executive of Anthropic will turn down an invitation to appear at a Senate committee hearing on AI this week, in the wake of the revelation that OpenAI agents had breached Australian government websites.

However, the company will make an appearance before another committee early next week.

The chair of the Senate inquiry into AI and datacentres, Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young, wrote to OpenAI and Anthropic last week asking for their US-based chief executives to appear before the committee on Thursday this week.

The invite came after the prime minister’s revelation that OpenAI’s agents had infiltrated systems run by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, Victoria’s Department of Health, the New South Wales Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research, and the Medicare statistics reporting service portal of Services Australia.

Neither company’s executives could be compelled to appear before the Senate committee, given they are based outside Australia, and it is understood that Anthropic – the company behind Claude – will not attend the hearing this week.

It is understood the company’s local team is not in Australia, and the invite was considered last-minute. An alternative date for the hearing has been sought.

Anthropic is, however, expected to attend a separate joint standing committee hearing on AI next week. Anthropic’s chief executive, Dario Amodei, will not attend, but it is understood representatives of its Australian and US operations will appear.

The company has made a submission to that committee in which Anthropic warned that governments had a critical role in reinforcing a responsible approach to AI by industry, while also arguing that frontier AI was not just an economic capability but also a “national security capability”.

“It matters which countries build the most capable models, and on whose terms they are deployed,” Anthropic said in the submission.

“The most capable AI models are built in the United States. Broadening that development out to trusted allies like Australia is critical and will support efforts to ensure that the capability of democracies outpace those of authoritarian states.”

OpenAI was approached for comment. The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, who was in the United States last week when announcing the hack, said he had spoken with OpenAI’s chief executive, Sam Altman, “to express Australia’s extreme concern about this incident”.

The finance and government services minister, Katy Gallagher, flagged new mandatory reporting rules could be introduced for AI data breaches. After criticism of the government’s slow response to the incident, Services Australia has put in place new procedures to ensure real-time monitoring of information sent to the public-facing email address used by OpenAI to report the hacking.

But Gallagher rejected Coalition claims the government had politicised the Medicare breach, rejecting suggestions Labor had delayed a public announcement or overstated the significance of the rogue agent’s actions.

“It is the first time that we’re aware that an agent acting on its own, not with the authority of OpenAI, was able to get into one of our data systems, and I think we did the right thing,” she said.

Cabinet was briefed on the ongoing investigation on Monday, as the company continued to cooperate with Services Australia and the intelligence agency, the Australian Signals Directorate.

Gallagher said the investigation would take a matter of weeks to be completed but confirmed the statistical website accessed in the incident had been decommissioned and the data transferred to a new portal.

The taskforce would also review how OpenAI’s agent had interacted with the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare’s website.

An obscure German wiki site that was reportedly hijacked and used as a message board for the agents to communicate with each other included messages showing the agents tried and failed to access the AIHW website data over multiple days in June this year, as first reported by the ABC.

Part of $160m in new funding for cybersecurity improvements at Services Australia, announced in the May budget, will be used for the response to the OpenAI incident.

“The kind of cyber protections of a public-facing website, versus our systems of government significance are quite different, and they are under constant, constant attention from people who would like to get in,” Gallagher said.

“Those systems are the ones that the upgrade will be focused on.”

The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, said every cyber-attack was serious, but criticised Albanese for waiting to reveal the incident publicly.

The semiconductor giant, which has been rapidly expanding its product lineup beyond chips, is rolling out two open-source software security tools that can be run on its hardware. They're designed to control what AI agents can access in real time and shut them down when they break the rules.

If cutting-edge labs had been using this technology to evaluate their AI models early on, it could have warded off the Hugging Face attack, Justin Boitano, Nvidia's vice president of enterprise AI, said during a briefing with reporters ahead of Monday's announcement. "From what we know, this new security platform could have stopped the breach," he said.

Misconduct by autonomous agents, including the Hugging Face incident in July, has roiled the AI industry and led to calls to slow down work on the technology. With the new product — dubbed the Open Agent Safety Platform — Nvidia is offering a way to prevent breaches without curbing AI development. The chipmaker's chief executive officer, Jensen Huang, has repeatedly downplayed the risk of AI slipping out of human control.

Boitano didn't comment on whether OpenAI or rival Anthropic PBC have plans to use its new system to monitor their training runs, deferring to the companies.

In recent days, Huang has cast safety concerns as an engineering challenge, rather than something that requires more regulation or global coordination. He joined US President Donald Trump in pushing back on assertions from some AI developers that the technology could lead to human extinction, but he also insisted that AI must be rigorously safety-tested.

Huang's engineering solution to the AI safety problem has two parts. OpenShell, a software product that Nvidia already previewed at its hallmark technology-focused conference in March, can run on Nvidia's Vera central processing units. It enables users to set rules for what AI agents can access and enforce them in real time. The software is open source, meaning it can be used and adapted freely.

title: British police investigate possible Iran link after arrests near U.S.-run base
description:
— Police were holding five men on Monday and examining suspected explosives found near a U.S.-operated air force base in England, as counterterror detectives investigated whether the arrests foiled an attempted attack linked to Iran.
The men were detained early Sunday after three vans were spotted near RAF Fairford, a U.K.
fullText:
FAIRFORD, England (AP) — Police were holding five men on Monday and examining suspected explosives found near a U.S.-operated air force base in England, as counterterror detectives investigated whether the arrests foiled an attempted attack linked to Iran.

The men were detained early Sunday after three vans were spotted near RAF Fairford, a U.K.-owned base that has been used by American bombers during decades of conflicts in the Middle East.

Investigators have not concluded whether the incident is a state-backed attack. They are investigating a possible link to Iran, Russia or non-state-backed militant groups. RAF Fairford has also been the focus of protests by anti-war campaigners.

The five suspects, who have not been named, were initially held over suspected explosives offenses, and later also arrested on suspicion of preparing an act of terrorism.

Police said the men are all British nationals from London and in their 20s. They can be held in custody for up to 14 days before they must be charged or released.

Residents were evacuated from 85 homes in the village of Whelford near the base on Sunday and army bomb-disposal experts used a robot to examine three white vans. The villagers had not been able to go home as of Monday morning, and the vans had not yet been moved.

President Donald Trump said the suspects had been detained following cooperation between the U.S. and Britain, and had been "under view" for some time. Police, however, said the arrests were triggered by a late-night call about "suspicious vehicles" near the base.

British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting declined to give details of the operation, but said "it was a proud moment" that Trump had recognized "the work that our police and intelligence services do every day."

"As and when we can, we will report back to the public about these individuals and about the nature of the threat," Streeting told Times Radio.

The arrests come at a time of heightened tensions around the threat from hostile states, with British intelligence services saying Russia and Iran have both used proxies to commit crimes on British soil. In March, officials said the number of national security cases involving activity by hostile states, including Iran, increased 50% in the six months to December 2025.

Britain did not join the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran that began Feb. 28 and initially denied Trump's request to use bases in the U.K. to strike Iran. But then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer agreed in March to let the U.S. use bases in Britain for what he called "defensive" operations against Iran's missiles and their launch sites following Iranian attacks on U.K. interests and Britain's allies in the Gulf.

American B-1 and B-52 bombers have taken off from Fairford, 100 miles (160 kilometers) west of London, for operations during the Iran conflict.

Iran has said it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target.

British security officials say proxies linked to Iran have been behind a string of arson and sabotage attempts in the U.K. and other countries, many of them targeting the Jewish community. They have previously warned that Tehran could expand its targets in the U.K. if conflicts in the Middle East continue.

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Monday that the incident is a "reminder of the threats our country faces."

Miliband met Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi at the United Nations in New York last week and told him that "Britain will not tolerate intimidation, threats or hostile activity on U.K. soil," according to a U.K. readout of the conversation.

The U.S. Air Force said its personnel based at RAF Fairford "remain vigilant," but "for operational security reasons we will not discuss specific force protection measures."

The U.S. Embassy in London has warned Americans in Britain to be cautious and mindful of their personal security.

Trump said authorities had the suspects "under view for a long time and we got them."

"It was an amazing job. We had them under investigation. They were looking to do big damage to our fort. And working with the British worked out great," he told reporters in Chicago on Sunday.

Lawless reported from Liverpool, England. Ben Finley in Washington contributed to this report.

title: Trump asked China's Xi if he wants to buy U.S. arms, ambassador says
description: — President Donald Trump has justified the pending U.S. arms sale to Taiwan to Chinese President Xi Jinping by downplaying it as just one of many sales Washington makes around the world — even asking Xi if he’d be in the market for U.S. arms, Trump’s ambassador to China said on Sunday.
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump has justified the pending U.S. arms sale to Taiwan to Chinese President Xi Jinping by downplaying it as just one of many sales Washington makes around the world — even asking Xi if he'd be in the market for U.S. arms, Trump's ambassador to China said on Sunday.

David Perdue said Trump raised the prospect of the arms sales from the U.S. to its ascendant geopolitical rival, an unlikely offer that if consummated would upend generations of U.S. policy toward China and Taiwan and potentially expose U.S. technology to a potential foe. Perdue, speaking to Shannon Bream on "Fox News Sunday" days after Trump hosted Xi for a state visit in Washington, didn't specify when the offer was made.

Bream had cited concerns from Republican and Democratic lawmakers over delayed aid packages and weapons orders to Taiwan, the self-ruled democracy, to defend itself from China's threat to invade the island. Bream asked if the U.S. is denying arms to Taiwan to appease the Chinese president, who visited Trump last week.

Perdue pushed back on the suggestion, stating that Trump "is as strong on Taiwan as I've ever seen anybody" and has sold it plenty of weapons. Perdue also said Trump and Xi continue to talk about future U.S. weapons sales to Taiwan.

"But President Trump continues to say, 'Hey, we sell arms to other people around the world,'" Perdue said. "He actually asked President Xi, would he like to buy some, at one point."

The U.S. is bound by its own laws to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself. While not recognizing Taiwan as a country, the U.S. is the island's strongest informal backer and arms provider. But multiple U.S. leaders have left ambiguous whether they would commit military force to defend the U.S. ally should China invade.

China has pressed Washington to halt the arms sales, most prominently during a previous summit in May between Trump and Xi in Beijing. After that meeting, the United States paused the sale of a record-breaking $14 billion package — and Trump described arms sales to Taiwan as a "very good negotiating chip" with China.

In their private talks at the White House last week, Xi pressed Trump to oppose Taiwan independence, according to Chinese state media.

In Beijing, China's foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun did not confirm Perdue's remarks when asked about the matter on Monday. But he told reporters that China has always strengthened its national defense capabilities based on its needs, and is committed to maintaining world peace and stability.

title: Iran says it's up to Trump to choose between war and diplomacy
description:
What to know about the Iran war today:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that Tehran is "fully prepared for the war to be resumed," and also for the possibility of renewed diplomacy with the U.S. aimed at ending the seven-month conflict, and it's "up to President Trump to choose."Mr. Trump told Axios on Sunday that he expected talks with Iran to resume this week, insisting again that the Islamic Republic is "losing badly" and eager to strike a peace deal.
fullText:
Iran has lodged a complaint with the United Nations over U.S. sanctions against its aviation sector, which have forced the cancellation of many flights across the region, state media reported Monday.

The U.S. imposed restrictions this month on the entire Iranian aviation industry and vowed to take a hard line against any companies or countries that continue to assist it.

As the sanctions took effect last Wednesday, some major airlines were forced to cancel international flights as several nations in the region implemented bans.

"To defend the legitimate rights of the aviation industry and counter illegal restrictions imposed by America, Iran has drafted and submitted a formal protest to the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO)," said civil aviation chief Abouzar Shiroudi, according to Iran's official IRNA news agency.

Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei has been quoted as predicting that U.S. military forces will soon be driven out of the Arabian Sea.

In a message to mark Iran's Sacred Defense Week, the ayatollah - who has not been seen or heard from directly since the war began - said U.S. forces were unable to advance beyond the Arabian Sea, which leads to the Strait of Hormuz, "because of the painful blows they have received."

He added that soon, U.S. troops would be driven from the Arabian Sea, too.

U.S. forces have operated across the region since the war began, including to escort commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz in defiance of Iran's bid to control traffic through the vital waterway.

The wide-ranging message attributed by Iranian state media to Khamenei included praise for Iran's military forces, as well as for the former leader of the Iran-backed Hezbollah group in Lebanon.

Khamenei was named Iran's new supreme leader soon after his father and predecessor, Ali Khamenei, was killed in the first round of U.S.-Israeli strikes, which sparked the war on Feb. 28.

The younger Khamenei has not been seen, even in video, since he was named the supreme leader, and senior U.S. officials have said he was likely seriously wounded in the same strike that killed his father.

The Iranian rial has fallen to a new historic low against the U.S. dollar, with the free-market selling rate surpassing 2.4 million rials per dollar on Monday.

Data from Pashizi, which tracks Iran's free-market exchange rates, put the dollar at around 2.4 million rials as Iran faces high inflation, sweeping sanctions and growing disruption to foreign trade.

Annual inflation has reached 61.4% in August, while food prices are reported to have risen 128% from a year earlier, according to data from Iran's Statistical Center .

Iranian state media said Monday that Iran's delegation at the U.N. General Assembly in New York had no plans to hold direct talks with the U.S., after President Trump said he expected more negotiations to take place this week.

"Iran's delegation in New York has no plans for negotiations with the United States," said the official IRNA news agency, citing an unnamed source close to the group.

Mr. Trump told Axios on Sunday he expected negotiations to continue this week, and added that the Iranian leaders were interested in reaching an agreement because they are "losing badly."

"Iran's views and positions were conveyed clearly and explicitly to the U.S. side... via a Qatari mediator," IRNA said, adding that the Iranian delegation would return to Tehran on Tuesday.

Since the outbreak of the war in February, negotiations between Tehran and Washington have occurred largely through mediators.

U.K. police said five men arrested in the early hours of Sunday near an air base used by the United States during its war against Iran were being held on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act that appeared to involve three trucks.

RAF Fairford, a U.K. Royal Air Force base about 85 miles west of London in rural Gloucestershire, has been used by American bombers to conduct strikes against Iranian missile sites. The British government, under an agreement made under former Prime Minister Keir Starmer, granted the U.S. permission to use Farford and other key U.K. bases provided it was only for strikes defined as defensive in nature.

Authorities are investigating a link between the arrests in Fairford and Iran as one possibility. Iranian authorities have declared all bases used to attack Iranian territory as legitimate targets.

President Trump praised those who were involved in making the arrests.

"It was an amazing job. We had them under investigation. They were looking to do big damage to our fort. And working with the British worked out great," he told reporters in Chicago on Sunday. "We had them under view for a long time and we got them."

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that Tehran was ready for either diplomacy or a return to fighting in the war sparked seven months ago by joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran. He said it is now up to President Trump to choose which direction to go.

"We are fully prepared for the time for the war to be resumed, and I repeat, we stand firm in the face of any new aggression, even if it comes to a doomsday war," Araghchi told NBC News' "Meet the Press."

"At the same time, we stand ready for diplomacy. It is up to President Trump to choose," he said.

President Trump on Saturday rejected Iran's proposal to return to a ceasefire agreement that collapsed months ago as part of a seven-day plan that would see it reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping.

Araghchi said Tehran would wait for an official response from mediators.

President Trump said Sunday that he expects talks with Iran to resume in the coming week, a day after he rejected a truce proposal put forward by Tehran.

"They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make," Mr. Trump told Axios in a phone interview on Sunday. "It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago."

Iran said Friday it had submitted a proposal to the U.S. to reopen the Strait of Hormuz over seven days, but Mr. Trump asserted that Iranian leaders wanted the deal because "they are losing so badly."

"They overplayed their hand," Mr. Trump told Axios.

The president said resuming strikes on Iran was not off the table, adding: "I am always thinking about it."

epublican Sen. John Kennedy of Louisiana said Iran's proposed plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart talks was "not a serious offer."

"The president's not Bambi's baby brother. He turned it down," Kennedy said Sunday on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan."

"We need to continue doing what we're doing — the sanctions, the blockade," said Kennedy.

"Now there's just one problem: The strait is at least partially closed, and it's affected the price of oil. And oil's in everything, including gasoline, and it's painful as hell," he said, adding: "We've got to either figure out a way to settle this thing, to get the strait open, or to escalate."

Kennedy said he would not support sending U.S. ground troops into Iran, however.

description: Browns fans booed Deshaun Watson in the second half of a preseason game against the Bills.
fullText:
Browns fans booed Deshaun Watson in the second half of a preseason game against the Bills. On Sunday, they cheered him.

Watson threw a 14-yard touchdown pass to tight end Harold Fannin Jr. with 1:48 left to lift the Browns to a 21-18 upset of the Panthers. He finished with 144 yards and two touchdowns, along with 45 yards rushing on 11 carries.

"It was great. It was amazing. I just wanted to finish the job for them," Watson said of the fans, via Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN. "There was one moment where I got a little teary-eyed, feeling that energy. I've put in so much work to get here, to be in this moment here and to be able to show I can finish these drives, and finish these games to get W's for this city and this organization.

"This is what all the hard work, belief, prayers, everything that I have put myself through the last 22 months. To be able to stand in front of the crowd on that field and to finish the job. I want to keep improving and keep trying to get better each and every day, each week and we have a big one on Thursday [against the Steelers]."

After the home fans booed him last month, Watson made it worse by calling it "disrespectful" and "personal." He apologized a few days later, saying his "emotions got the best of me."

The only way to win them over was to play well and win, and Watson has done both.

The Browns are tied for first place with the other three teams in the division at 2-1, and Watson has completed 63.8 percent of his passes for 587 yards with five touchdowns and one interception. He also has run for 105 yards.

He is the first Browns quarterback since Baker Mayfield in Weeks 14 and 15 of 2018 to lead game-winning touchdown drives in the fourth quarter of consecutive games, according to ESPN Research.

"We continued to feed off that energy of the crowd, and we wanted to make a special play," Watson said. "I told the guys in the huddle, 'Man, just [believe] in me and I'm going to use my legs.' Whenever that play comes up, make that play, and Harold did."

title: Browns Face Growing Jerry Jeudy Problem After Week 3 Win
description: The Cleveland Browns are facing a growing problem with Jerry Jeudy after he was shut out again. The post Browns Face Growing Jerry Jeudy Problem After Week 3 Win appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Cleveland Browns have won two straight games, and Jerry Jeudy hasn't caught a pass in either one.

Jeudy did not draw a target in Sunday's 21-18 victory over the Carolina Panthers, leaving the veteran receiver with two catches for 26 yards through three games. Both receptions came in the season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

His latest empty afternoon came after Mary Kay Cabot of cleveland.com reported that the Browns were not looking to trade him. Cleveland's plans to keep Jeudy and its apparent inability to get him involved are becoming an increasingly uncomfortable combination.

"The Browns are also not contemplating trading Jerry Jeudy, even though he has only two catches for 26 yards, both from Week 1 in Jacksonville. Last week in Tampa, Jeudy was targeted once, but it was on a throwaway in the fourth quarter," Cabot said before Sunday's game.

That leaves Jeudy with one target over Cleveland's past two games — and even that throw offered little opportunity to make a play.

Cabot said the Browns would remain open-minded about an offer they could not refuse, but they were not seeking to weaken a receiving corps they believed could help them win. That said, Jeudy's trade value is not going to get any better if he's not involved whatsoever in the game plan.

Cleveland's younger pass catchers have taken on prominent roles, with rookie receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston joining tight end Harold Fannin Jr. as key options for Deshaun Watson.

Fannin was the difference against Carolina, catching seven passes for 51 yards and both of Watson's touchdowns. Boston added two catches for 41 yards and secured the two-point conversion following Fannin's go-ahead score.

Watson attempted 30 passes. None went Jeudy's way, despite being on the field for nearly every passing opportunity.

There's no doubt the passing game has room for improvement. Watson finished with just 144 passing yards, and the Browns needed a late touchdown drive to avoid dropping their home opener.

Cleveland could use another dependable option as Watson settles into head coach Todd Monken's offense. But consecutive games without a reception establish that Jeudy's limited production extends beyond one quiet afternoon.

The Browns acquired Jeudy from the Denver Broncos in 2024 and signed him to a three-year extension. His first season in Cleveland offered plenty of reason to believe that investment would pay off.

Jeudy earned a Pro Bowl selection after catching 90 passes for 1,229 yards and four touchdowns. His production dropped to 50 receptions for 602 yards and two scores in 2025.

Through three games this season, he has yet to approach the role he held during that breakout year.

title: Season Ends for Rockies With Loss to White Sox
description: The Colorado Rockies wrapped up the 2026 MLB season as the postseason-bound Chicago White Sox secured a victory.
fullText:
The 2026 MLB season came to an end for the Colorado Rockies on Sunday afternoon and, unfortunately, it ended with a loss.

Colorado finished its season with a 58-104 season record. It was not the season that the Rockies, players, or fans wanted to see happen. Yes, there were some things that were good to look at and others, well, not so much.

On Sunday at Rate Field in Chicago, the Chicago White Sox defeated Colorado 4-2. Kyle Freeland got the start for Colorado and he took the loss. His season record ends up at 4-12, going four innings and giving up seven hits, four earned runs, no walks, two strikeouts, and surrendering two home runs.

Mark Manfredi, Nick Frasso, and Jaden Hill came out of the Rockies' bullpen to put the stops to a Chicago offense that took control of this series.

Connor Norby's sacrifice fly in the top of the third inning set Colorado up with an early 1-0 lead. Chicago, though, bounced right back with a four-run third and took a 4-1 advantage.

Cole Carrigg, who had a heck of a season, put the Rockies' final run on the board this season with his 13th home run in the top of the eighth inning.

The Rockies were 0-for-2 with runners in scoring position and left four total runners on base. As for the White Sox, they were 2-for-10 with runners in scoring position and left six total runners on base.

Norby, Carrigg, Kyle Karros, Adael Amador, and Jordan Beck were the only hitters for Colorado to get base hits in Game No. 162.

Let's break down what the 104 losses mean for the Rockies this season. They are tied for the second-most in franchise history along with the 2023 Rockies, but the team also had a 15-loss improvement over last season's team that finished 43-119.

Yes, this is the fourth straight season that the Rockies have lost 100-plus games. In 2024, Colorado was 61-101 and the 2023 Rockies were 59-103. This season's squad finished up going 3-17 in its last 20 games going back to Sept. 6. Now, since Aug. 17, Colorado finished up 8-30.

Those are hard numbers to look at for a franchise looking to turn things around. Some of the Rockies' young players in the Pacific Coast League earned recognition, so there might be some hope of future help.

What does the future, though, look like for the pitching situation? That will be worth keeping an eye on in the offseason.

For now, Rockies fans, this season is over. A lockout looms over the start of the 2027 MLB season. If that's avoidable, then Spring Training will come around before you know it.

fullText:
UConn football had a third win in its grasp, but let it slip away. Despite some stumbles through four quarters, the Huskies had multiple possessions with a chance to pull ahead in the game's final minutes and couldn't make the final plays to secure a victory.

After decisively building a 14-0 lead, offensive production spiraled downward, with just seven points in the second half and declining yardage as each quarter went on. Though it wasn't a bad performance overall, UConn still heads home with a sour taste after a game it could have won.

Thoughts as UConn falls to 2-2 with Syracuse visiting the Rent this Saturday:

With the game tied at 21 in the fourth quarter, UConn had the ball after forcing a three-and-out. A sack on first down set the back, and on 3rd & 10, Kalieb Osborne threw an interception on an errant throw, giving the home team the ball in enemy territory. This helped them put up a field goal that ended up being the game-winning points.

The Huskies had one more chance down three to tie the game or take the lead, but again a penalty sent them back and the drive stalled. Their inability to respond after losing the lead is concerning.

Ultimately, allowing Miami to storm back into this and then hold on even after the RedHawks' starting QB David McComb left with an injury makes this a disappointing outcome. The team stayed in the battle, but really fell flat after such a strong start through the first seven minutes.

After a quiet start, McComb began connecting deep in the second and third quarter, eclipsing 300 passing yards in the fourth quarter before his leg injury. Some of his receivers made some big plays, including an amazing one-handed grab by a tight end, and UConn also conceded a defensive pass interference call that led to the equalizing touchdown.

In total, seven defensive backs took the field and recorded at least one tackle. Of the seven players, six had hardly played a full game before coming to UConn and earning a starting role. This is going to be an area that opponents will continue to attack.

For the second consecutive week, Bowers led the running backs in yards, while Osborne was the team's leading rusher. Week after week, it is clear that the powerful runner is getting more comfortable and finding the hole more easily. In four games, Bowers has racked up 186 rushing yards for three touchdowns.

Touchdown! 💪 pic.twitter.com/o2q18ldVfy

Inexperience is showing on the O-line as well. The Huskies allowed three QB hurries and two sacks. Of their six penalties for 60 yards, false starts and holding on the line were three of them. These drive-killers really hurt Jason Candle's squad in a close contest.

Tiger Woods kept a watchful eye on Team USA from afar during the Presidents Cup. Like every other American golf fan, he was pleased with how things turned out.

Woods made a rare statement on social media shortly after the Americans completed a furious Sunday singles comeback to defeat the International team and capture their 11th straight Presidents Cup title.

"What a comeback! Congrats to Team USA on an incredible Presidents Cup victory," Woods tweeted on Sept. 27. "They needed all the matchups to go their way and they got it done. Great team win."

Woods, of course, had an accomplished Presidents Cup career of his own. The Americans went 7-1-1 in Woods' nine Presidents Cup appearances, and his 27.5 points are second on the all-time points list. While the Americans suffered their one and only Presidents Cup loss in Woods' debut in 1998, his career with the event came full circle in 2019. Woods went 3-0 as a playing captain, leading the Americans to a win in a return to Royal Melbourne — where the Americans suffered that lone defeat.

Woods' future with Team USA remains uncertain. He was poised to lead the Americans in the 2027 Ryder Cup at Adare Manor in Ireland. That was before Woods announced he was stepping away from golf following a car crash and subsequent arrest in March.

title: Rafael Jodar gives his honest opinion of Jannik Sinner as a person
description: Jannik Sinner has already established himself as a tennis great and is well on his way to becoming a legend of the sport. With five...
fullText:
Jannik Sinner has already established himself as a tennis great and is well on his way to becoming a legend of the sport.

With five Grand Slam titles to his name at 25 years of age, the Italian has more majors than the likes of Andy Murray and Stan Wawrinka. He has captured 30 tour-level crowns, including 10 ATP Masters 1000s, and has spent a total of 90 weeks at world number one, a tally that ranks 10th all-time.

His rivalry with Carlos Alcaraz is special for many reasons, but mainly because of how different they are, both on and off the court. Sinner is certainly the more reserved of the two, though not much is known about what he's like behind the scenes.

Rafael Jodar, the 20-year-old Spaniard who burst onto the scene during the clay swing this year, gave his view of Sinner as a person in a recent interview with La Repubblica. "He's really a good person, funny and incredibly humble," said Jodar.

"He's missed by everyone on court. I hope he'll come back soon". Sinner has played Jodar once on the ATP Tour, with the sole meeting coming at the Madrid Open earlier this year. In the quarterfinals of the ATP Masters 1000 tournament, Jodar fell to Sinner in straight sets, despite testing him in the second by forcing a tiebreak.

Sinner is currently sidelined with a knee injury that forced him to withdraw from Montreal, Cincinnati, the US Open and Beijing. His last appearance on the ATP Tour came in the Wimbledon final, where he beat Alexander Zverev to capture his fifth Grand Slam trophy.

In his absence, Zverev has closed in on Sinner's position at world number one by winning the US Open, his second major. The German can clinch the top spot in the rankings by winning the Shanghai Masters, but he would need Sinner to withdraw from the tournament.

Despite winning two Grand Slam titles this year and potentially becoming the world number one, Zverev has a record of two wins and eight losses against top 10 players in 2026. He has failed to beat either Alcaraz or Sinner this season, with five straight defeats to the latter.

After withdrawing from the China Open, Sinner still has three title defences between now and the end of the season. The first comes at the Vienna Open, which he won for the second time in three years in 2025.

The next will come at the Paris Masters, which, if he pulls out of Shanghai, will mark Sinner's first appearance at an ATP 1000 event since the Monte-Carlo Masters. Sinner won each of the first five Masters 1000 events of the season in Indian Wells, Miami, Monte-Carlo, Madrid and Rome.

Sinner's third and final title defence will be the hardest: the ATP Finals. He won the year-end tournament for the second time in a row last year by beating Alcaraz in the title bout. If he wins again this season, he will become the fourth player in history to three-peat at the ATP Finals, joining Ilie Nastase, Ivan Lendl and Novak Djokovic.

title: Carlos Alcaraz wants to make one ‘request’ to tennis chiefs after what happened at the Laver Cup
description: Carlos Alcaraz played another very important role for Team Europe as they reclaimed the Laver Cup from Team World. Alcaraz finished the tournament with a...
fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz played another very important role for Team Europe as they reclaimed the Laver Cup from Team World.

Alcaraz finished the tournament with a 100% record, winning his one singles match and one doubles match in London. He earned one point for a doubles win with Jakub Mensik against Alexander Bublik and Taylor Fritz, and two points for a singles win over Fritz. The Spaniard was scheduled to play against Alex de Minaur on day three of three, but Alexander Zverev claimed the Laver Cup title for the hosts before then.

The winning Laver Cup team gathered for a press conference after the victory, where both Mensik and Alcaraz were tasked with discussing the speed of the courts at the event. The O2 arena in London played host to the hard-court, indoor ATP event, where no ranking points are available, but matches count towards head-to-head records.

Told the conditions looked slow and difficult to play in, Mensik and Alcaraz were asked for their opinions on the matter. It was also suggested to the pair that indoor tennis allows players to attack more, with the duo asked what it was really like and if they think it should be different in the future.

Mensik replied: "Well, yeah, obviously, especially me or I guess all of us, we felt like the conditions were pretty slow, which, yeah, compared to the other tournaments, it's one of the probably slowest surfaces that I have played on this year, like as far as hard courts are here.

"So yeah, I mean, it was really tough for me to get used to it, to get the rhythm. Especially for me, my game is a lot about the serve and heavy groundstrokes. It's even more difficult for me to finish the ball. So, you know, the trend of this, I didn't really know where it's going, but obviously with the combination of the balls, which I consider them that they were not that good, as well, it was super slow."

And Alcaraz commented: "I mean, for me, I don't mind slow courts. You know, especially with my serve, it's not the biggest one. No, but yeah, in terms of, you know, I mean, I have been talking with Yannick [Noah], the team, how the tennis has improved over the years, how fast it was the courts back then. And now, you know, it's getting slower, but I think it's not about the courts. It is about the balls, I would say.

"You know, we can see during a lot of tournaments how the balls' reaction from the court is totally different. The ball becomes super big, and it's a totally different game when it's new balls. We play two or three games with those balls, you have to adapt yourself the best you can.

"I don't know where if they're going to change it or not, but what I request is that they have to see the best ball possible for the courts are made, the tournaments we're going to play. I think that's a really important thing to know. But, you know, who knows? What I can say is I'm trying to adapt myself and the game the best I can in the tournament that I go."

It remains to be seen whether or not Alcaraz's request will be granted, but he clearly isn't the only player having an issue with the balls being used. But he is one of many top players who must quickly move on amid the busy ATP calendar, where there is very little time to try and make a successful switch from tournament to tournament and court to court.

That is a skill Alcaraz has mastered throughout his glittering career so far, which takes him to Tokyo next. Alcaraz loves the Laver Cup, but he now returns to more competitive action at the Japan Open, where he is the defending champion.

title: 32 things we learned in NFL Week 3: Bills don't look good, literally or figuratively
description: Every season, the team's winless and undefeated teams draw a lot of scrutiny after two weeks – uet that script tends to flip, as it did Sunday in Washington.
fullText:
The 32 things we learned from Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season:

0(-3). That would be a reference to the league's winless teams, of which there are five (Houston Texans, Miami Dolphins, Los Angeles Chargers, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Tennessee Titans) now saddled with that weighty record − one only seven teams in league history have overcome to make the playoffs. The Texans managed to do it in 2025, but no club has ever pulled it off in successive seasons. (But worth noting that Houston is the only team in the 21st century to surmount the 0-3 challenge, also pulling it off in 2018.)

1. Back to that familiar question that's pervaded the early part of the 2026 season: Who's No. 1? It's now a tough case to make for the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks after they lost at Washington to a team without its starting quarterback. The Buffalo Bills were fortunate to survive the winless Chargers, QB Josh Allen playing a terrible game in a terrible uniform … more on those fronts later. The undefeated San Francisco 49ers? Can they field a functional team next week? Ready to make a case for the Las Vegas Raiders or Minnesota Vikings, who are also 3-0? Ready to re-anoint the dynastic Kansas City Chiefs ... despite a fairly ugly win at feckless Miami? Check nfl.usatoday.com on Tuesday morning once the dust has fully settled … and our next batch of power rankings are out of the oven.

1a. Prior to Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro, the Dallas Cowboys had appeared in one international game – the fewest in NFL history. But they may have also participated in the best international game in league history. Keep reading ...

(QB)2: Kudos to backups Marcus Mariota and Jameis Winston, who led the Commanders and New York Giants, respectively, to wins Sunday – a week after both teams lost their starting quarterbacks, the Giants' Jaxson Dart expected to miss the rest of the season. Next up? Chicago Bears veteran backup Case Keenum, who is expected to start Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles in place of injured Caleb Williams.

3(-0). Five teams currently sport that spotless record (49ers, Bills, Chiefs, Raiders and Vikings). Philly can join their ranks Monday night with a win at Soldier Field.

4. The number of consecutive seasons an 0-2 team knocked off a 2-0 team, which happened Sunday when the Commanders ambushed the Seahawks, who won 38-14 at Northwest Stadium last November. And the upset came amid Seattle QB Sam Darnold's return from his Week 1 gluteal injury − and he played his butt off Sunday with 379 yards and four TDs through the air.

5. The number of turnovers committed by the Bills on Sunday, three courtesy of Allen. It was Buffalo's first win with that many giveaways since 1997. Good thing Buffalo's defense finally showed up, even if the Bolts offense didn't ... again.

5a. Ugly a game as he had, Allen became the first QB in NFL history with multiple rushing TDs in three consecutive games.

6. The number of TD receptions by Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who's excelling, per usual, no matter which of his quarterbacks is throwing to him. The 2025 Offensive Player of the Year is on a very early pace to shatter Hall of Famer Randy Moss' single-season record (23 TD grabs in 2007).

Jaxon Smith-Njigba has had 120+ receiving yards and 1+ receiving TD in each of his team's first 3 games 🫨

The only other player to accomplish that in NFL history is HOF Jerry Rice@Seahawks | #GoHawks pic.twitter.com/nVNt719IkI

7. However it appears the Detroit Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs is going to give JSN a run for his money when it comes to capturing 2026 OPOY honors. Gibbs, who posted 164 yards and three touchdowns from scrimmage in Sunday's 31-24 defeat of the New York Jets, is off to a historic start.

.@Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs is the first player in @NFL history to produce the following statistics through the first 3 games of any season:

- 300 rushing yards
- 4 rushing TDs
- 150 receiving yards
- 2 receiving TDs#OnePride pic.twitter.com/YGj3AZSIMe

8. The jersey number of four-time NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers, who passed for at least 290 yards (292) and multiple TDs (3) for the first time as a Pittsburgh Steeler in Sunday's 30-27 escape from the Cincinnati Bengals, who still haven't started 3-0 since 2015.

9. Number of consecutive games lost by the Indianapolis Colts, the longest skid in the league going back to last season … prior to Sunday's narrow victory over Houston.

10. Weird zero stat of the day: Cleveland Browns backup QB Shedeur Sanders completed his only pass of the day for 0 yards. That translates to a passer rating of 79.2, which is significantly better than Carolina Panthers counterpart Bryce Young's on Sunday (70.7, even though Young completed 26 of 48 passes for 291 yards, a TD and an INT). Sanders' 79.2 would have even led the league back in the old, pre-Super Bowl era (before 1966) days.

11. Weirdest zero stat of the day: Niners WR Deebo Samuel had 80 receiving yards and a TD in Sunday's win … despite finishing with zero receptions. Explanation? He scored the game's first touchdown on a hook-and-lateral with WR Mike Evans, who was credited with a 2-yard catch on the play.

HOOK-AND-LADDER TD 🤯

Deebo Samuel traveled a total distance of 110.35 yards and reached a max speed of 20.39 MPH on this 80-yard touchdown, per @NextGenStats @AZvsSF on FOX/FOX One
Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/88dsZtSZum

11a. Samuel also iced San Francisco's 36-30 victory over the Arizona Cardinals with another uncredited catch.

Deebo ices it on the hands team 👏@AZvsSF on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/t32MJ70YM6

12. Number of consecutive games won by the Seahawks, the longest heater in the league going back to last season … prior to Sunday's loss to the Commanders. Seattle failed to become the third consecutive Super Bowl champion to begin its title defense with a 3-0 start.

13. Alternate uniforms < throwback uniforms.

It's merely a rule of thumb, not an immutable law. But if you saw the Bills ("Nickel City") and Colts ("Anvil Strike") unis on Sunday, then you'd probably agree that gray is a good color for baseball roadies … not so much for NFL uniforms.

The @BuffaloBills' "Nickel City" uniforms are ready for their debut. @LACvsBUF on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SWjFLvF6Jw

14. However the Jacksonville Jaguars' throwbacks? Sweet. Can we get those back as the primaries?

The Jaguars "Prowler" throwbacks should be their primary uniforms. I will die on this hill without regrets. pic.twitter.com/7b7Sj2Kyhq

15. Speaking of bad looks, what's the tougher watch on TV: Indy's Lucas Oil Stadium with the roof open on a sunny day – like Sunday – or AT&T Stadium with the sun streaming through its western end-zone windows?

16. The Cowboys didn't have to deal with any glare – or even a bad field – Sunday while facing the Ravens at Maracanã Stadium in the league's first foray into Rio. But their problematic defense sabotaged them yet again – surrendering a 27-yard completion to Zay Flowers on the game's final game from scrimmage … before Ravens K Tyler Loop drilled the game-winning 56-yarder to secure a 34-31 victory. Still, this was a fantastic game and, who's to say, perhaps a Super Bowl 61 preview based on how this unpredictable season has unfolded so far.

17. Congratulations to Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter, who notched his first career interception Sunday … albeit on a – another – terrible throw by New England Patriots QB Drake Maye. Ten games into his career, Hunter, the insanely hyped dual-threat, Heisman Trophy-winning star from the University of Colorado, has one career pick and one career TD. I've been as skeptical as anyone about his pro prognosis, but good to see a player – and a great young man by many accounts – have a highlight moment.

TRAVIS HUNTER FIRST CAREER INT ‼️@NEvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tZFgPtUIf4

18. Did you know Jacksonville has a Brian Thomas Jr. and Bryan Thomas Jr. on its roster? Brian, the better-known wideout, had one catch for 8 yards in the Jags' 35-6 rout of the Patriots. Bryan, a defensive end, was credited with a tackle and half-sack of Maye.

19. Jaguars K Cam Little, who hit a 70-yard field goal in preseason last year and also broke the official record with a 68-yarder in the regular season last November, nearly hit a 70-yarder that counted right before halftime Sunday … but was wide right by inches. It's coming, though.

Cam Little attempts a record-breaking 70-yard field goal but it is no good.#NFL pic.twitter.com/obwBsaikJF

Cam Little thought his 70-yarder was good against the Patriots:

“Out of the 67, the 68, and the 70 that I’ve attempted, I by far hit that ball the cleanest by a mile.”#Jaguars #DUUUVAL @BrentASJax pic.twitter.com/3t6bA9wCZm

20. "Browns are gonna Browns?" Admittedly, I poked fun at first-year Cleveland coach Todd Monken for getting worked up about NBC analyst Mike Tomlin's dig prior to the Browns' win at Tampa last week. But maybe it's a positive phrase? Whatever you think of QB Deshaun Watson on a human level, he's got his team off to a 2-1 start after engineering Sunday's fourth-quarter win over the Panthers.

21. "Kinda poetic that I get this highlight," Tomlin said, the longtime Steelers coach, said on "Football Night in America," while breaking down the Browns' second consecutive win.

22. Watson, who's been a reviled figure in Cleveland essentially since his disastrous 2022 acquisition, was actually cheered Sunday, including when he returned after missing a play on a roughing penalty that preceded his game-winning TD pass to TE Harold Fannin Jr.

23. "I got a little teary-eyed feeling that energy because I put so much work to get back here, to be in this moment, to show that I can finish these games and get W's for the city and this organization," Watson said following the win.

24. The undefeated Raiders have already matched last season's win total (3), which is what allowed them to draft QB Fernando Mendoza atop the 2026 draft.

25. Not that Las Vegas has needed the 2025 Heisman Trophy winner as veteran Kirk Cousins has tossed three TDs in all three of the Silver and Black's victories, including Sunday's come-from-behind effort in New Orleans.

26. That's because the Saints had been dominant in the fourth quarter, outscoring opponents 25-3 in the final period over the first two weeks. But the Raiders outpointed them 13-0 in the fourth in Sunday's 35-27 win at the Superdome.

27. And while second-year Saints QB Tyler Shough threw four TD passes Sunday, he also turned the ball over three times, giving Cousins and the Raiders the margin for error they needed to snatch the victory.

28. Call the Raiders' start fluky if you want, but remember that Sunday was the first game this season in which they had, arguably, their best player – TE Brock Bowers making his 2026 debut to the tune of 10 catches, 116 yards and a TD. He missed the first two weeks after undergoing a meniscus trim.

29. Call the Vikings' 3-0 start fluky if you want – especially in light of injuries to QB Kyler Murray, WR Justin Jefferson (Sunday) and others. They also needed a punt return for a TD in their 23-16 win at Tampa on Sunday. But that Minnesota D is vicious – racking up six sacks and 12 QB hits Sunday while knocking Bucs QB Baker Mayfield from the game.

30. If you didn't know, Mayfield's backup is undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who threw a pick among three incompletions in his pro debut. The Bucs' ship sure appears to be sinking fast while going to the bottom of the NFC South standings, especially after Mayfield suffered a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand.

31. A reminder to all NFL players, officials and writers: "You guys better get your (expletive) together" … which is what referee Ronald Torbert told his crew (on a hot mic) during Sunday's game in Indianapolis, per the Associated Press.

32. Last and, sadly, least – the Dolphins. Not only are the Fins winless, they haven't come closer than 14 points to a victory. Perhaps worse, RB De'Von Achane, their best player, suffered a knee injury that seems to be serious, coach Jeff Hafley admitting a lack of optimism about Achane's prognosis. Could we be witnessing the first 0-17 outfit in NFL history?

All the NFL news on and off the field.

title: Why Tom Brady called Justin Herbert interception a ‘meatball sub’
description: Keeping up with the youths is no easy task. The meaning of words can change without any of the olds being aware of the switch, leaving those out of the know in troubled waters. Thankfully, for those of us a step or two behind in football’s latest trends, we have Tom Brady to keep us…
fullText:
Keeping up with the youths is no easy task.

The meaning of words can change without any of the olds being aware of the switch, leaving those out of the know in troubled waters.

Thankfully, for those of us a step or two behind in football's latest trends, we have Tom Brady to keep us up to date.

In the booth for Fox alongside Kevin Burkhardt to call Sunday's game between the Los Angeles Chargers and Buffalo Bills, Brady sounded disappointed in Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert after he threw an ugly pick over the middle.

"Herbert trying to throw down the middle of the field to Valdes-Scantling, but there's a safety in the middle of the field. That's Gardner-Johnson," Brady said over the replay. "Poor awareness. Poor decision. Throws him a meatball sub."

Tom Brady: “Herbert trying to throw down the middle of the field… But there’s a safety in the middle of the field… Poor awareness. Poor decision. Throws him a meatball sub.” #NFL pic.twitter.com/5XzEAxnr8V

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) September 27, 2026

The term "meatball" has been in the sports world for some time — in baseball it refers to a pitch thrown right down the middle for an eager hitter to hit out of the park — but the meatball sub phenomenon in football is not as well established.

At the start of the season, several social media posts began referring to interceptions as "meatball subs," or other various sandwiches. Some early posts seem to indicate the meme references the idea that throwing such interceptions might lead to taking a job as a sandwich artist, but now it's simply used to refer to a real bad pick. Like so many similar language quirks, context dissolves pretty quickly.

The interceptions-as-sandwiches bit is not entirely new, but it undoubtedly hit a new level of popularity at the start of the 2026 season.

A sampling of those jokes, or a hoagie tray, if you will.

bo nix starting early pic.twitter.com/nVZnSLH7wd

— hopps (@HoppsSzn) September 15, 2026

Drake Maye when he throws more then 10 yards pic.twitter.com/nn3wvwvVzP

— 8 Bal® (@LamarDummy) September 10, 2026

chicken bacon ranch sub on toasted white bread with sunchips on the side pic.twitter.com/v6et4jJsH2 https://t.co/BSV3p30PYr

— Tyler (@HighAsTy) September 15, 2026

DESHAUN WATSON MEATBALL SUB ON THE THIRD PLAY OF THE GAME pic.twitter.com/lUTDci7BtW

— DaRealConMan (1-1) (@darealconman) September 13, 2026

The key aspect of making an interception a meatball sub is that it is an interception for which the quarterback is entirely to blame. Given how many interceptions are caused by tipped balls or simply great plays by defenders, there's a case to be made that meatball subs should be their own statistical category.

That said, if the slang term has reached a saturation point that it is being used in the broadcast booth by Tom Brady, there's a chance the moment is already over.
